newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot propane steady to higher late trade.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot propane steady to higher late trade.

text.p: U.S. spot propane prices were steady to higher in light activity late on Tuesday amid weak NYMEX futures and cold weather in the Midwest.
Players said the declining values of NYMEX December crude oil futures softened the U.S. Gulf Coast, which jumped up early this morning before easing back down at midday.
In late trade, Mont Belvieu, Texas, spot propane was largely steady at between 54.25 cents and 54.50 cents a gallon.
In the Midwest continuing crop drying demand and cold weather added strength to the market.
Conway, Kansas, hub material traded at 55.50 cents, a quarter cent higher than at midday.

A few traders said several petrochemical companies were easing off propane to buy normal butane because of a two cent spread. A spread below five cents makes normal butane more economical than propane to crack.
Belvieu normal butane was valued unchanged at 55.75/56.00 cents, while Conway material remained 55.00/55.25 cents.
-- Laney Salisbury, New York Energy Desk +1 212 859 1631
